statute: The Cosmetics Rules, 2020 & Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940
title: Regulatory Boundary: Ayurvedic Cosmetics vs. Ayurvedic Drugs
content:
Section 3(aaa) defines a cosmetic as any article intended to be rubbed, poured, sprinkled, or sprayed on, or introduced into, or otherwise applied to the human body for cleansing, beautifying, promoting attractiveness, or altering appearance.

The Critical Ayurvedic Distinction:
1. If an Ayurvedic formulation (e.g., Kumkumadi Tailam, Aloe Vera gel) is marketed solely to moisturize, cleanse, or beautify skin, it is regulated as a Cosmetic.
2. If it claims to cure acne, eczema, psoriasis, or regrow hair, it crosses into an ASU Drug requiring a drug manufacturing license under Rule 154.
3. IP Posture: Formulation compositions for cosmetics face heavy Section 3(p) objections; novel delivery systems (e.g., liposomes) or trademark branding are the primary viable IP routes.
